question: A quadratic polynomial with real coefficients and leading coefficient \(1\) is called disrespectful if the equation \(p(p(x)) = 0\) is satisfied by exactly three real numbers. Among all the disrespectful quadratic polynomials, there is a unique such polynomial \(\tilde{p}(x)\) for which the sum of the roots is maximized. What is \(\tilde{p}(1)?\)
solution:
The key observation is that a solution of \(p(p(x))=0\) must make \(p(x)\) equal to a root of \(p\).

The polynomial \(p\) must have real roots; otherwise the composition has no real zeros. It cannot have just one repeated root \(r\), because then \(p(p(x))=0\) reduces to the quadratic equation \(p(x)=r\), which has at most two distinct solutions. Thus write
\[
p(x)=(x-r)(x-s),\qquad r\ne s,
\]
with \(r,s\) real. Now
\[
p(p(x))=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
p(x)=r\ \text{or}\ p(x)=s.
\]
These equations have no common solution, since \(r\ne s\). For their solution counts to total three, one quadratic must have exactly one distinct real solution and the other exactly two. Name the roots so that \(p(x)=r\) has the single solution.

Expanding that equation gives
\[
x^2-(r+s)x+r(s-1)=0.
\]
Its discriminant must be zero, so
\[
0=(r+s)^2-4r(s-1)=(r-s)^2+4r.
\]
Because \(r\ne s\), this forces \(r<0\). Set \(r=-t^2\), where \(t>0\). The discriminant equation then yields
\[
s=-t^2\pm2t.
\]
Consequently, the sum of the roots satisfies
\[
\begin{aligned}
r+s&=-2t^2\pm2t\\
&\le-2t^2+2t\\
&=\frac12-2\left(t-\frac12\right)^2\\
&\le\frac12.
\end{aligned}
\]
Equality requires the plus sign and \(t=\tfrac12\), giving \(r=-\tfrac14\) and \(s=\tfrac34\). These determine a unique monic polynomial:
\[
\tilde p(x)=\left(x+\frac14\right)\left(x-\frac34\right)
=\left(x-\frac14\right)^2-\frac14.
\]
We must check that it is disrespectful. The equation \(\tilde p(x)=-\tfrac14\) gives only \(x=\tfrac14\), while \(\tilde p(x)=\tfrac34\) gives \(x=\tfrac14\pm1\). Thus the composition has exactly three distinct real zeros, as required.

Finally,
\[
\tilde p(1)=\left(1+\frac14\right)\left(1-\frac34\right)
=\frac54\cdot\frac14=\boxed{\frac5{16}},
\]
which is choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
